core_traits.srd_text: With a nearby trainer, you advance one level and increase your maximum hit points by your hit point gain per level.
When you enter an area of darkness, you gain the In Darkness condition. It lasts while you remain in that darkness.
Spend 1 ability score improvement point to increase your Charisma by 1, up to 20.
Spend 1 ability score improvement point to raise your Constitution by 1, up to 20. If this increases your Constitution modifier, your maximum hit points increase for each level you have.
Spend 1 ASI point to increase your Dexterity by 1, up to 20. Your Armor Class increases if this raises your Dexterity modifier.
Spend 1 ability increase point to raise your Intelligence by 1, up to 20.
Spend 1 ability score improvement point to raise your Strength by 1, up to a maximum of 20.
Spend 1 ability increase point to raise your Wisdom by 1, up to 20.
Strike a creature within your reach using an equipped melee weapon. Add your proficiency bonus and the weapon’s relevant ability modifier to the attack, then deal the weapon’s damage on a hit.
Make a melee attack with a weapon that has Graze. On a hit, deal its normal damage; on a miss, deal damage equal to your Strength modifier.
Make a melee attack with a Sap mastery weapon. On a hit, you deal damage and hinder the target’s next attack until the start of its next turn.
Make a melee attack with a weapon that has the Slow mastery. On a hit, you deal damage and reduce the target’s Speed by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
Make a melee attack with a weapon that can topple foes. On a hit, you deal damage and knock the target prone.
Make a melee attack with a Vex weapon. When you hit, you deal damage and gain advantage on your attack rolls until the start of your next turn.
You make a weapon attack without choosing a target. The action is spent, but nothing is struck.
When a creature you can see leaves your reach, you can use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it with a weapon or Unarmed Strike.
Make an attack with a ranged weapon against a target within its normal range. Add your Dexterity and proficiency bonus to the attack roll, then deal the weapon’s listed damage on a hit.
Once on each of your turns, add extra damage to a hit with a finesse or ranged weapon when you have an edge on the attack or an active ally is close to the target.
Make a melee attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, it takes bludgeoning damage equal to 1 plus your Strength modifier.
You attune your awareness to nearby threats. While it lasts, you have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against dangers you can perceive.
As a bonus action, you spend a use to become raging until the start of your next turn.
At the start of your turn, you can attack recklessly to gain advantage on your attacks. Until your next turn begins, attacks against you also have advantage.
You spend a use as a Bonus Action to inspire a creature you can see within 60 feet, giving it Bardic Inspiration.
Spend your banked Bardic Inspiration die to remove it and gain a brief bonus to ability checks.
A Dexterity check that measures balance, agility, and control. You make it when you try to stay upright, move through tight spaces, or perform a difficult maneuver.
Make a Wisdom check to calm, train, direct, or understand an animal. The GM calls for it when your handling could affect the animal’s behavior.
An Intelligence check that draws on magical knowledge. You use it to recall lore about spells, enchanted objects, magical symbols, and other arcane phenomena.
A Strength-based check for climbing, swimming, jumping, grappling, or other feats of physical power. You make it when the outcome depends on training, endurance, or force.
A measure of your force of personality, confidence, and social presence. You make this check when those qualities determine whether you succeed.
A measure of your endurance and physical resilience. You make this check when you must push through strain, fatigue, or other bodily demands.
Make a Deception check when you try to mislead someone with lies, disguises, or false intent. The result shows how convincing your deception is.
A test of your agility, balance, or reflexes. You make it when no specific Dexterity skill applies.
Recall historical events, cultures, and legends. You make this check when past knowledge could help you understand a person, place, object, or situation.
You use this check to judge a creature’s motives, emotions, or honesty from its behavior and words.

Use this when you try to recall information, reason through a problem, or make sense of something without relying on a specific skill. The GM may call for it when your intellect alone determines the outcome.
Make a Charisma check to cow, threaten, or force someone to back down. The result determines how strongly your pressure affects them.
You search for clues, hidden details, or useful information. The GM calls for this check when careful examination could reveal something.
Use thieves’ tools to pick a lock. Make a Dexterity check against DC 15, adding your proficiency bonus if you’re proficient with the tools or Sleight of Hand.
An ability check using Wisdom to assess injuries or illness, provide first aid, or identify the cause of death. You make it when medical knowledge or treatment matters.
Make an Intelligence check to recall or recognize information about plants, animals, weather, terrain, and other natural phenomena.
You use this check to notice hidden details, creatures, sounds, or other changes in your surroundings. Make it when the GM asks whether you detect something.
Use this check when you entertain an audience through music, dance, acting, or another performance. The result shows how well you hold their attention or move them.
Make a Charisma check to influence someone through tact, honesty, or a convincing argument. Use it when your words could change a creature’s attitude or decision.
You call on your knowledge of gods, sacred traditions, rituals, and religious symbols to answer a question or recognize their significance.
You make a Dexterity check to perform delicate manual tricks, conceal an object, or lift something unnoticed.
Make this check when you try to move unseen or unheard. Your result determines how well you avoid notice.
A measure of your physical power. You make this check when brute force, lifting, pushing, or resisting force matters.
You make a Survival check to track creatures, find food or shelter, or navigate the wilderness. You use it when your knowledge of natural environments matters.
A Wisdom check measures your awareness, instincts, or judgment when no specific skill applies. Roll it when the GM calls for a test of those qualities.
When a creature dies, you claim the experience it was worth if no one has claimed it yet.
You spend a Channel Divinity use to force a creature to make a Constitution save. On a failed save, it takes radiant damage; on a success, it takes half as much.
You spend a use of Channel Divinity as a Magic action to restore hit points to a creature you can see.
You spend a use of Channel Divinity to restore hit points to a bloodied creature you can see within 30 feet. The amount restored equals five times your cleric level.
You spend a use of Channel Divinity to repel Undead within 30 feet. Each affected creature becomes Frightened and Incapacitated.
You make a clear statement to a creature. This has no rules effect unless another feature gives it one.
You silently send a message to a living creature within range, addressing them at their current location.
As a bonus action, you drink a potion or use another consumable you are carrying. Choose the item: it loses one dose and its effect takes hold of you.
You spend your action to gain extra movement for the current turn.
At the start of your turn with 0 Hit Points, make this free check. Three successes make you Stable, while three failures kill you.
You focus on avoiding harm until the start of your next turn, making attacks against you less likely to succeed.
You spend a use to exhale destructive energy over an area. Creatures there make a Dexterity save, taking damage on a failure.
You expend a use of Wild Shape to summon a cat familiar in your space. It serves as though called by the familiar-summoning spell, without using a spell slot.
You use a bonus action and spend one use of this feature to assume a beast form. You cannot change directly from one form to another.
On your turn, spend a use to gain one additional action this round. You can’t use that action to take the Magic action.
You attune to a remarkable feat of athletic skill, gaining the Remarkable Athlete condition.
Spend one use as a bonus action to regain hit points based on your fighter level.
You assist a nearby ally with an ability check. Until the end of your next turn, they have help on their next check using a proficiency you choose.
Spend one Heroic Inspiration after rolling an eligible die to reroll it. You use the new result.
In place of one attack, you hurl a vial of acid at a creature within 20 feet. Unless it succeeds on a Dexterity save, it takes acid damage. The vial is used up either way.
In place of one attack, you throw a flask of alchemist's fire at a creature within 20 feet. Unless it succeeds on a Dexterity save, it takes fire damage. The flask is used up either way.
You spill ball bearings from their pouch where you stand. For a minute, each round every creature there, you included, must make a Dexterity save or fall prone. The pouch is used up.

You spread caltrops from their bag where you stand. For a minute, each round every creature there, you included, must make a Dexterity save or take 1 piercing damage and be unable to move until the start of its next turn. The bag is used up.
In place of one attack, you throw a flask of holy water at a creature within 20 feet. A fiend or undead that fails a Dexterity save takes radiant damage. The flask is used up either way.
Spend 1 charge to cast fireball at its base power. Resolve the spell normally.
Spend 1 charge to cast magic missile at its lowest level. Resolve the spell normally.
You prepare to turn aside an incoming strike. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack that hits you is deflected automatically.
Spend 1 Focus Point to make an Unarmed Strike as a bonus action. If you have Open Hand Technique, a hit can prevent the target from making opportunity attacks until its next turn begins.
After you take the Attack action with a monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can use your Bonus Action to make one Unarmed Strike.
Spend 1 Focus Point to Dodge as a bonus action. Until your next turn, attacks against you are less likely to hit, and you have an edge on avoiding certain effects.
When you fall, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage you take by an amount based on your level.
Spend 1 Focus Point and a Bonus Action to Dash. Your movement for the turn increases by an amount equal to your speed.
Spend 1 Focus Point to take the Disengage action as a bonus action.
You attune yourself to unarmored movement, gaining its speed bonus while you meet its requirements.
You give yourself the Prone condition without spending an action or Speed, unless your Speed is already 0.
While prone, you can spend movement equal to half your Speed to stand. You must have enough movement remaining to do so.
You spend one use of your Channel Divinity to fuel a paladin feature that calls for it.
You spend a 1st-level spell slot as a bonus action to deal radiant damage to the target.
You spend 5 points from your healing pool to restore 5 hit points to a creature you touch.
Spend 1 point from your healing pool to restore 1 hit point to a creature you touch.
Spend 10 points from your healing pool to restore 10 hit points to a creature you touch.
You take an item that is lying on the ground, or sitting loose inside an open container, into your own hands.
You spend one use of this feature to activate one of your Favored Enemy options.
After at least 8 hours of qualifying downtime, you complete a Long Rest. If you are Resourceful, you gain Heroic Inspiration.
You declare that you have finished at least 1 hour of qualifying downtime. This marks the end of your short rest.
You use a bonus action to move again this turn, gaining extra movement equal to your speed.
You use a bonus action to move without provoking opportunity attacks for the rest of your turn.
As a bonus action, you gain advantage on your next attack before your next turn begins.
You use a bonus action to take the Utilize action or make a Sleight of Hand check.
You gain a climbing speed, letting you move up, down, and across climbable surfaces without slowing.
You expend a 1st-level spell slot to gain 1 sorcery point.
You expend a 2nd-level spell slot to regain 2 sorcery points.
You spend 2 Sorcery Points as a bonus action to create a 1st-level spell slot.
As a bonus action, you spend 3 Sorcery Points to create a 2nd-level spell slot. You can use this option once you reach 3rd level in this class.
You use a bonus action and expend a use to empower your innate magic for a limited time.
You spend 1 Sorcery Point to prepare a spell with Careful Spell when you cast it.
You speak aloud at your current location without choosing a specific listener. Anyone there can hear you.
Speak to a living creature at its current location. The creature hears you, and others in the same place may overhear.
You speak to someone loudly enough for everyone nearby to hear. Each creature in the room receives your words from its own position.
You cast Mage Armor on yourself without spending a spell slot.
Spend 1 minute in a rite to regain expended Pact Magic spell slots, up to half your maximum number, rounded up.
After a short rest, you can regain expended spell slots with a combined level up to half your wizard level, rounded up.
When your experience reaches the next advancement threshold, you can gain one character level and apply your class’s level benefits.
When you enter a dark area, you gain the effects of being in darkness until you leave it or the area becomes lit.
Make an attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. You use it when you take the Attack action.
When you defeat a creature, you can claim the Experience Points it is worth.
You speak, signal, or otherwise convey a message. This has no mechanical effect unless another rule says it does.
You communicate aloud to creatures near you. Your spoken words can be perceived by those who can hear you.
You mentally address a creature within range, even without sharing its space. You cannot reach through barriers that block this contact.
You can drink a potion or use another consumable you carry on yourself; a potion takes a Bonus Action to drink.
When you take this action, you gain extra movement equal to your Speed for the rest of the turn.
When you take this action, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the turn.
You focus on avoiding harm until your next turn. Attacks against you are less likely to hit, and you are better at Dexterity saves, unless you are incapacitated or cannot move.
You exhale destructive energy in a short cone or long line. Creatures in the area make a Dexterity save against your Breath Weapon DC, taking damage on a failed save.
On your turn, you can make yourself Prone without using an action or spending any Speed.
You use your action to aid another creature’s ability check or attack, or to provide first aid.
After you roll for an uncertain outcome, you can spend Heroic Inspiration to reroll one die when a reroll is allowed.
You try to stay unnoticed by making a Dexterity (Stealth) check. Use it when you move carefully, conceal yourself, or avoid drawing attention.
You try to shift a creature’s attitude with charm, threats, performance, deception, or animal handling. Make the appropriate Charisma or Wisdom check.
After at least 8 hours of qualifying downtime, you complete a Long Rest and regain the benefits tied to it. If you have the Resourceful trait, you also gain Heroic Inspiration.
You use your action to cast a spell, activate a magic item, or use a magical feature that requires an action.
You can pick up a loose item on the ground, or loose inside a container within reach, as one of your turn's free object interactions.
You prepare an action and choose a trigger. You use that action as a reaction when the trigger occurs.
Make a Wisdom check using Insight, Medicine, Perception, or Survival to look for clues, creatures, or other hidden details.
You cast See Invisibility to reveal unseen creatures and objects around you for a limited time.
After at least 1 hour of qualifying downtime, you complete a Short Rest and trigger effects that occur when it ends.
You spend movement equal to half your Speed to stop being Prone.
You make an Intelligence check using Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion to learn or recall useful information.
Use a nonmagical object that calls for an action to operate, such as opening a door or activating a mechanism.
You gain a Climb Speed, letting you move up, down, or across suitable surfaces without spending extra movement.
You can see in darkness as though it were dim light, though colors appear only as shades of gray.
While unconscious, you make this check at the start of each of your turns. Three successes make you stable; three failures kill you.
You can move through the air using your flying speed. Use it when a rule or movement path allows flying.
You can see creatures hidden by invisibility as though they were visible, so they gain no attack advantage or protection from you for being unseen.
You can move through water using your swimming speed when a rule or effect allows you to swim.
You can move across ordinary ground and through spaces you can normally enter. Use it when moving on a tactical grid or between connected places.
You can attempt an Acrobatics check when balance, agility, or controlled movement is relevant. Whether you add your proficiency bonus depends on your training.
You can make an Animal Handling check when you try to influence, calm, or understand an animal. Your proficiency applies if you have it.
You can attempt Arcana checks when the rules call for them. Whether you add your proficiency bonus depends on your Arcana proficiency.
You can attempt an Athletics check when the GM calls for one. Your proficiency, if any, is applied by the Athletics skill itself.
You can attempt a Charisma check when the rules call for one. Proficiency, if applicable, is determined separately.
You can attempt a Constitution check when the rules call for one. Your proficiency, if applicable, is determined separately.
You can make Deception checks when you try to mislead someone through words, behavior, or a false presentation. Your proficiency, if any, applies separately.
You can attempt a Dexterity check when the task calls for agility, balance, coordination, or quick movement.
You can make History checks when recalling or interpreting past events, people, and cultures. Your proficiency, if any, applies as normal.
You can attempt an Insight check when you try to read a creature’s motives, behavior, or trustworthiness.
You can attempt an Intelligence check when a task calls for reasoning, recall, or analysis. Proficiency applies only if another rule grants it.
You can make an Intimidation check when you try to frighten, coerce, or cow someone. Whether you add your proficiency bonus depends on your training.
You can make an Intelligence check using Investigation when you try to uncover clues, analyze details, or deduce how something works.
A tool check you make to open a lock without its key. Use it when you try to bypass a locked door, chest, or similar mechanism.
You can attempt checks that use the Medicine skill when the rules or GM call for one.
You can attempt checks that use your knowledge of natural environments, plants, animals, and weather.
You can make a Perception check when you try to notice something using your senses. Whether you add your proficiency bonus depends on your training.
You can make a Performance check when you try to entertain, impress, or convey emotion through a performance.
You can attempt to influence someone through tact, charm, or honest appeal when the situation calls for it.
You can make Intelligence checks to recall religious traditions, rites, symbols, and divine lore.
You can attempt Sleight of Hand checks when the rules call for careful manual work or misdirection.
You can make a Stealth check when you try to avoid notice or move without drawing attention.
You can attempt a Strength check when a task calls for raw physical power, force, or endurance.
You can make a Survival check when you try to track creatures, navigate wild places, or understand natural signs.
You can attempt a Wisdom check when the rules call for one. Any proficiency bonus comes from the relevant skill or other feature.
You gain an edge on Dexterity saving throws against effects you can see, as long as you are not blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
While raging, your first hit with a Strength-based attack each turn deals extra damage equal to your Rage Damage.
As a bonus action, you enter a battle fury that grants its listed benefits for a limited time.
At the start of your turn, you can fight recklessly to gain advantage on Strength-based melee attacks that turn. Until your next turn, attack rolls against you also have advantage.
You inspire an ally, giving them a die they can spend after rolling to improve a check, attack, or saving throw.
You call on sacred power to produce a Channel Divinity effect granted by your class or subclass. You use it to choose from options such as healing, harming, or driving away undead.
When you cast a spell using a spell slot that restores hit points, each creature healed regains additional hit points equal to 2 plus the spell’s level.
You use your Channel Divinity to restore a large amount of hit points to a wounded creature that is below half its hit point maximum.
You use a Magic action and expend a use of Wild Shape to summon a familiar without providing material components. The familiar is a Fey spirit in animal form.
You magically take on a beast’s form for a limited time. You use it to gain that form’s movement and physical abilities, returning to your normal form when the effect ends.
On your turn, you can spend an Action Surge use to gain one additional action that turn.
You add half your proficiency bonus to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution checks that do not already include it. Your jumps also cover more distance.
As a bonus action, you draw on your stamina to regain Hit Points. You can use it again after you finish a short or long rest.
While you are ready to deflect, you reduce damage from one attack that hits you each turn by an amount based on your Dexterity and monk level.
Your unarmed strikes use your Martial Arts die and your choice of Strength or Dexterity. After you attack with an unarmed strike or monk weapon, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.
You spend Focus Points to fuel Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind.
When you fall, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage you take by five times your monk level.
Your speed increases while you aren’t wearing armor or using a shield. The bonus grows as you gain monk levels.
You draw on sacred power to fuel a Channel Divinity option granted by your oath. You can use it only when an option tells you how to spend it.
After you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use a bonus action and expend a 1st-level spell slot to deal extra radiant damage to it.
You draw on a pool of healing power to restore a creature’s hit points. Choose how much to spend, up to the power you have remaining.
Choose a type of creature you know how to track and fight. You gain special advantages when recalling information about it or pursuing it through the wild.
You can use a bonus action to Dash or Disengage on your turn.
As a bonus action, you give yourself advantage on your next attack this turn. You can use it only if you have not moved, and your speed becomes 0 until the turn ends.
You can use Utilize as a bonus action, or make a Sleight of Hand check as a bonus action.
You climb at the same speed you walk.
You know a secret language used to share messages with other criminals and rogues. You can understand it and use it to communicate discreetly.
You convert sorcery points into spell slots, or expend spell slots to regain sorcery points. The spell slot’s level determines the points gained or required.
You can draw on your innate magical power to heighten your spellcasting. When you activate it, you gain its benefits for a short time.
Once between long rests, you can perform a brief rite to regain some of your expended pact magic. You use it when you have time to prepare but cannot complete a long rest.
Once between long rests, you recover expended spell slots during a short rest. The slots you regain have a combined level based on your wizard level.
You can cast Mage Armor on yourself without expending a spell slot.
Your training makes you exceptionally skilled at Acrobatics. When you make an Acrobatics check using your Proficiency Bonus, you add it twice.
Your training with Animal Handling lets you add twice your Proficiency Bonus to checks you make with that skill.
Your training lets you add double your Proficiency Bonus to Arcana checks you make.
Your training makes you especially reliable at Athletics. When you make an Athletics check, add twice your proficiency bonus.
Your training in Deception lets you add twice your Proficiency Bonus to checks you make with that skill.
Your training in History is exceptional. When you make a History check using your proficiency, you add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your training makes you especially reliable at reading people. When you make an Insight check using your proficiency, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your proficiency bonus is doubled for Intimidation checks you make.
Your training lets you apply double your Proficiency Bonus to Intelligence checks using Investigation.
Your training sharpens your medical knowledge. When you make a Medicine check using your proficiency, add twice your proficiency bonus.
Your training in Nature is exceptional. When you make a Nature check using your proficiency, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your training lets you add twice your Proficiency Bonus to Perception checks you make with this skill.
Your training in Performance lets you add twice your Proficiency Bonus to checks you make with that skill.
Your training makes you exceptionally persuasive. When you make a Persuasion check, add twice your proficiency bonus.
Your training sharpens your knowledge of religion. When you make a Religion check using proficiency, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your training makes you exceptionally deft. When you make a Sleight of Hand check using your proficiency, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your training makes you exceptionally capable at moving unnoticed. When you make a Stealth check, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
Your training makes you especially reliable at tracking, foraging, and navigating. When you make a Survival check using your proficiency, add twice your Proficiency Bonus.
This feat lets you improve one of your ability scores when you gain an Ability Score Improvement. Choose it to unlock the available score increases.
You add your proficiency bonus to initiative rolls.
You expend charges from a Wand of Fireballs to cast Fireball.
You expend charges from a Wand of Magic Missiles to cast Magic Missile.
When you cast a spell that forces saving throws, you can spend 1 sorcery point to protect chosen creatures from its effects if they succeed on the save.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with alchemist’s supplies. You use them to create and identify alchemical substances.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with brewer’s supplies. You use them to produce and assess fermented drinks.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with calligrapher’s supplies. You use them to create and assess fine writing, lettering, and official documents.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with carpenter’s tools. You use them to build, repair, or assess wooden structures and objects.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with cartographer’s tools. You use them to create, study, and copy maps.
You add your proficiency bonus when you make checks using cobbler’s tools to craft or repair footwear.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with cook’s utensils. You use them to prepare food and perform related culinary tasks.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a dice gaming set. Use it when you play, cheat at, or assess games of chance.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with glassblower’s tools. You use them to shape, repair, and assess glass objects.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with jeweler’s tools. Use them to work with gems, precious metals, and fine jewelry.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with leatherworker’s tools. You use them to craft, repair, or assess leather goods.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with mason’s tools. You use them to shape, repair, and work stone.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with bagpipes. You can use them to perform music or support related tasks.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a drum. You can use it to perform music, keep rhythm, or support related tasks.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with a dulcimer when it applies.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a flute.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a horn. You can use it to perform music, signal others, or create similar sounds.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make while playing or using a lute.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a lyre.

entries.display_name: Tool Proficiency: Musical Instrument, Pan Flute

core_traits.srd_text: You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a pan flute.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with a shawm. You can use it to perform music or apply your musical training.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with a viol.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with painter’s supplies. You use them to create, repair, or study painted works.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with potter’s tools. You use them to shape, fire, and repair ceramic objects.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with smith’s tools. Use them to shape, repair, or assess metal items.
You add your Proficiency Bonus to checks you make with thieves’ tools.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with tinker's tools. You use them to repair, assemble, and identify small mechanical devices.
You add your proficiency bonus to checks you make with weaver’s tools. You use them to make, repair, or assess cloth and woven goods.
You add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make with woodcarver’s tools. Use them to shape, carve, and repair wooden objects.
Your ability to keep your balance, move through tight spaces, and perform agile stunts when the situation calls for it.
Your ability to calm, train, or direct animals. You use it when you try to influence an animal’s behavior.
Your knowledge of magic, enchanted objects, and other planes. You use it to recall lore and identify magical phenomena.
You use this skill to make demanding jumps, swim through dangerous water, or force open and break sturdy objects.
Your ability to mislead others with lies, false appearances, or convincing disguises when someone might question what they see or hear.
Your knowledge of past events, notable people, nations, and cultures. You use it to recall lore and recognize historical context.
Your ability to read a creature’s mood and intentions. You use it when you study someone’s behavior for clues.
You use forceful presence, threats, or displays of power to pressure someone into doing what you want.
You search records for hidden information or study clues to work out how something functions.
You can examine a creature to identify an illness or learn the cause of a recent death.
Your knowledge of the natural world. You use it to recall lore about terrain, plants, animals, and weather.
Your ability to spot hidden details, unusual activity, and other things that might escape notice. You use it when your senses could reveal something important.
You use it to entertain an audience through acting, storytelling, music, or dance.
Your ability to influence others through tact, honesty, and a convincing manner. You use it when trying to win someone’s trust, agreement, or cooperation.
Your knowledge of religions, sacred rites, deities, and holy symbols. You use it to recall relevant lore.
Your knack for nimble fingerwork and misdirection. You use it to lift small items, hide objects on your person, or perform subtle tricks by hand.
Your ability to avoid notice by moving quietly and using cover or concealment. You use it when you try to hide, sneak past others, or move without drawing attention.
Your ability to navigate the wilds and read signs in nature. You use it to track creatures, gather food, find routes, and avoid environmental dangers.
You can’t make opportunity attacks. This ends at the start of your next turn.
You have an inspiration die from a bard. You can spend it after an ability check to gain a brief bonus to that check.
You have a bonus from a spent Bardic Inspiration die. Add it to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw before the start of your next turn.
You cannot see. Attacks you make are harder, and attacks against you are easier.
While charmed, you cannot harm the creature that charmed you. That creature has an easier time influencing you in social interactions.
You are maintaining a spell effect that requires your focus. When you take damage, make a Constitution saving throw or lose this condition and end the effects it supports.
You have an edge on Dexterity saving throws. This benefit applies even while you are incapacitated.
You are a corpse and are Incapacitated. A monster becomes Dead at 0 Hit Points; a character becomes Dead after three failed Death Saving Throws.
You cannot hear. A check that needs hearing fails.
You have already used Deflect Attacks this turn. The effect ends at the start of your next turn.
While this is active, the next attack that deals damage to you is reduced by your Dexterity modifier plus your monk level and a roll. It ends after reducing damage.
While this lasts, attacks against you are less likely to hit, and you have an edge on Dexterity saving throws. It ends at the start of your next turn.
While you are Dodging, you have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
You are worn down. Each level of exhaustion makes d20 tests and speed worse, until six levels end you.
